thread:
lucy.ng: Heads-up — we're seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures between eu-west-edge (proxy) and apac-model-runners after the RBAC push earlier. KMS logs show a lot of DecryptDenied for the rotator/service account. Happened ~4:03 UTC.

dinesh.r: Copy. Do you have sample logs / KMS request IDs? Also which PR changed RBAC?

lucy.ng: Here are the top lines from proxy logs + KMS snippet:
```
2026-03-21T04:03:12Z proxy[ingress-pod-7f9]: tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: internal error
2026-03-21T04:03:12Z proxy -> apac-runner: POST /infer 502 upstream handshake failed
KMS: RequestId=abc-1234 Status=Denied Principal=svc-rotator@redwood-prod Role=proxy-keystore-rotator Action=KMS:Decrypt
```

samir: That aligns with the RBAC terraform that landed in PR 11234 (rolled minimal perms). It tightened the rotator SA and accidentally removed kms:Decrypt on the proxy-keystore role binding. I can revert quickly.

katie_m: Quick question — are we sure it's not an expired cert on the apac side? handshake error is generic. Can someone run an s_client against the runner? Also check TLS session ticket settings (we had that session-resume change last month).

deploy-bot: PR 11234 merged by hannah at 2026-03-21T03:58:07Z — changelog: tighten service account scopes for rotator.

lucy.ng: Ran openssl quick check, certs look valid and not expired. Output:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect apac-runner.example.internal:443 -servername apac-runner.example.internal
SSL-Session:
    Protocol : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
    Verify return code: 0 (ok)
```
So cert expiry is NOT the issue. KMS denies look like core cause.

dinesh.r: Good catch. Plan: do a quick rollback of the RBAC change for proxy-keystore-rotator (temp grant kms:Decrypt), then run a canary traffic test EU->APAC. If that fixes handshakes, we know RBAC was the culprit. Samir can you apply the rollback and @lucy.ng can you run the canary?

samir: On it. Patch I'll apply (terraform) — adding back decrypt on the binding: 
```
# pseudo-terraform snippet
resource "iam_binding" "proxy_keystore_rotator" {
  role = "roles/kms.decrypter"
  members = ["serviceAccount:proxy-keystore-rotator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
```
I'll push a hotfix and post the plan.

lucy.ng: Doing the canary now, running 100 requests through eu-west to apac-runner canary pool.

lucy.ng: Canary results: 100/100 success after re-apply. TLS handshake errors dropped to zero. Looks fixed.

dinesh.r: That confirms root cause = RBAC deny. Next actions:
- revert PR 11234 fully until we itemize the minimal perms per region.
- add a cross-region RBAC gate in deploy pipeline (block if change touches kms bindings)
- add an alert for KMS DecryptDenied spikes (per-region) to SRE runbook
- add audit query for retrospective analysis

katie_m: Also: add an entry to the cert/mTLS checklist — before RBAC tightening that affects keystores, run a simulated decrypt check from each region. We should also document session ticket and TLS1.3 resumption implications when key unwrap is affected.

samir: I'll submit PR to revert and then a follow-up PR to rework perms with a canary rollout. I'll add a pre-merge CI job that runs a synthetic KMS decrypt with the affected SA against a test key. Example check command (GCP style):
```
gcloud kms keys versions decrypt --key key-name --location global --ciphertext-file /tmp/ciphertext --plaintext-file /tmp/plaintext --impersonate-service-account=proxy-keystore-rotator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Equivalent AWS/Azure ops will be added in the job.

lucy.ng: For audit/forensics, here's a quick KQL-like audit query I ran to surface affected regions and principals:
```
resource.type="kms_key" AND protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND protoPayload.status.code=7
| stats count() by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, resource.location
```
It showed concentrated denies from eu-west proxies to apac-runner keystores.

dinesh.r: Great. We should also add longer retention for these denies for 30 days under security retention so we can correlate with infra changes. Also escalate to compliance — they may want a short RCA since regions were impacted. I'll open the incident and assign owners.

katie_m: One more operational tweak: add a fallback path on proxy: if KMS decrypt for live key fails, try the local cache (if within TTL) and fall back to a lower-perf but available cipher path. That reduces blast radius for short-lived config errors.

lucy.ng: Filed incident INC-2026-0321-01, assigned to @dinesh.r and @samir for updates. I'll post a short incident summary to #incidents and notify affected infra owners.

samir: PR 11236 posted (revert). Rolling out now with canary 10% -> 100%, monitoring handshake metrics and KMS deny alerts.

lucy.ng: All green. Rolling to 100%. Will follow up tomorrow with a postmortem draft covering: root cause (RBAC tighten removed KMS:Decrypt), detection (KMS deny spike + handshake errors), mitigation (rollback + RBAC gate), and prevention (pre-merge KMS check, fallback cache, alerting tweaks).

dinesh.r: Thanks team. Quick wins: add pipeline blocker, add KMS deny alert per-region, update runbook. Longer term: perms review + canary automation. :thumbsup:

katie_m: Thanks — once postmortem is up I'll link to the mTLS checklist and perf tradeoffs doc.

deploy-bot: Deploy 11236 succeeded at 2026-03-21T04:12:55Z

lucy.ng: Closing thread; will ping when postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:"
